description: AERPAW at North Carolina State University publishes this experimental collection. The rural campaign records UAV signals at heights of 40, 70 and 100 metres. At 40 metres, sampling rates of 5, 10 and 20 MHz correspond to bandwidths of 1.25, 2.5 and 5 MHz. Five fixed nodes, LW1 through LW5, record dual-channel I/Q samples, GPS positions and received signal strength in SigMF files. DataCite describes B210 receivers; one landing equipment block names B205, so the equipment inconsistency is retained. Coverage is limited to the described experimental campaign. The linked Dryad release is registered under CC0 1.0 and is publicly accessible without charge. Formats and variables are described by the provider; the files were not downloaded. Caveats include campaign-specific equipment and conditions, which limit transfer to other networks. Simulation use: Rural air-to-ground channel calibration. Related records include the NSF PAWR testbed platform, which describes the wider experimental infrastructure.
